name: host shell backend
claim: A session's shell tool can run on a host exec target (WSL user or container) while its name, schema, description and result shape stay byte-identical to the in-browser machine.

models.result: Real bridge on Windows, 2026-11-20, targets wsl: (user wh) and wsl-podman: (container wh-dev, user dev); all 38 checks of the run held (both targets, the limits, and the page). Per call about 0.35 s (wsl) and 1.8 s (container). node --check app/main.js status 0; git status --short status 0; exit 7 with both streams in order; 3 s timeout answered in 3.3 s / 4.7 s with no process left in the distro or the container; dropped request stopped; 1.3 MB whole, 21 MB cut at 4,000,000 and marked; fifth concurrent call refused. From the page: tools and first message byte-identical on both targets; result text the same as the machine's. Limits found: a container whose process 1 does not reap keeps stopped commands' children as defunct entries (start it with --init); the tmux option could not be switched on with the in-page machine off until vmTmux became a Paste config field; with tmux each command is still its own bash (cd and export do not carry), as in the in-page machine. Not measured: a real model, docker, a Linux-run bridge against a container, macOS.
